sources.enabled: Add the sun at all. The exported scene's own lights are spot lights hung 3 m above the golfer; their cones end a few metres out, so on the 400 m ground the far turf was lit by the camera headlight alone at a grazing angle and read nearly black (down-the-line flight review, 2026-11-21).
sources.direction: Direction the light travels (x, y, z in the world frame, z up). Mostly downward (about 17 degrees from the vertical) so the surface normal of level ground makes the same angle with the light everywhere: a directional light has no position, so the turf is as bright at 300 m as at the tee. A low sun would darken the far ground again.
sources.color: Linear RGB of the light, a very slightly warm white.
sources.intensity: Scales the colour into the diffuse term. Measured on the matched driver address frame, down-the-line wide view, 1280x720 (mean pixel level, 0-255): near turf (rows 600-700) 23 without the sun, 35 at 0.4, 44 at 0.7; far turf just below the horizon (rows 330-380) 21, 33 and 41. 0.4 left the horizon band visibly darker than the turf at the golfer's feet; 0.7 lights the turf evenly to the horizon. The price is a near turf that is brighter (about 1.9x in level, same hue) and a shadow of the golfer with less contrast.
sources.castshadow: The sun draws no shadow map. The key light already shadows the golfer, a second shadow from another direction doubles the shadow of the body and its saw-tooth fringes on lit skin (see engines/physics_engines/mujoco/python/scene_lighting.py).
